bug_description.original_source: ARVO-Meta.report.comments[0].content / staged vulnerable source checkout / patch.diff / saved Stage 01 sanitizer trace
bug_description.normalized: The saved witness is the exact 29-byte file `7b 22 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 3a 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 22 3a 5b 74 72 75 65`. `json_reader::read_buffer()` copies all 29 bytes into its vector-backed `buffer_`, then resizes that vector to logical size 29 while retaining the 16384-byte reserved container seen in the ASan allocation stack. The parser later enters the first object member-name string, and because `JSONCONS_ILLEGAL_CONTROL_CHARACTER` only rejects `0x00..0x1f`, the raw `0x7f` bytes survive to the closing quote. `parse_string()` / `end_string_value()` / `visit_key()` forward that member name as `s = buffer_.data() + 2`, `length = 20` into `jsoncons::detail::escape_string()`, so `end = buffer_.data() + 22`. On each visited `0x7f`, `unicode_traits::to_codepoint()` returns `r.ptr = it + 1`, but the vulnerable statement `it = r.ptr;` runs inside `for (...; it != end; ++it)`. When the final visited key byte at `buffer_[21]` is `0x7f`, `it = r.ptr` sets `it == end`; the loop header then increments to `buffer_.data() + 23`, skipping the closing quote at `buffer_[22]`. Because the loop condition is only `it != end`, the loop keeps dereferencing bytes past the key slice but still inside the same 29-byte reader buffer, reading `:`, `[`, `t`, `r`, `u`, `e` at offsets 23..28. The next iteration dereferences `buffer_.data() + 29`, the first byte past the vector's logical size, which matches the saved AddressSanitizer container-overflow at `0x62900000021d` (29 bytes into the 16384-byte region). The fix changes the iterator update to `it = r.ptr - 1`, so the header performs the only advance and the loop stops at `end` instead of walking into the trailing buffer bytes.

source.description: First project read that materializes the attacker-controlled witness into the vector-backed reader buffer that later both backs the key slice and defines the 29-byte container boundary reported by ASan.
source.value_from: The saved file `gt_results/arvo_33781/poc` is exactly 29 bytes: `7b 22 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 3a 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 22 3a 5b 74 72 75 65`. `fuzz_json_encoder` wraps those bytes in a `std::istringstream`, and this project read copies all 29 bytes into `buffer_`, so `count == 29` before the vector is resized to that logical length.
source.note: Scored source step. This is the first project statement that turns the PoC bytes into vulnerability-relevant in-memory state.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. After the buggy loop has already left the 20-byte key slice and walked the trailing `:[true` bytes in the same 29-byte reader buffer, this dereference reads `buffer_.data() + 29`, the first byte past the vector's logical size.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `container-overflow READ of size 1` at `include/jsoncons/json_encoder.hpp:52:23` on address `0x62900000021d`, which is 29 bytes into the reader buffer's reserved 16384-byte region.

root_cause.description: Off-by-one iterator update. `to_codepoint()` already returns the first byte after the decoded code point, but `escape_string()` stores that pointer in `it` inside a `for (...; it != end; ++it)` loop; on the last key byte this leaves `it == end`, so the header advances to `end + 1` and the loop keeps running outside the key slice.
root_cause.note: The bundled fix changes this statement to `it = r.ptr - 1`, which leaves the loop header to perform the single intended advance and stop at `end`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Materializes the exact `(pointer,length)` key slice inside the 29-byte reader buffer. That slice later becomes the `string_view` passed to `visitor.key()` and then the `s,length` pair consumed by `escape_string()`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: After `parser_.update(buffer_.data(), 29)`, the saved witness reaches the closing quote at byte 22 with `sb == buffer_.data() + 2` and `input_ptr_ - sb == 20`, so the key slice is `buffer_[2..21]` and its exclusive end is `buffer_.data() + 22`.

parser_admitted.description: After consuming `{` and the opening quote of the first object member, the parser commits to the member-name string path and invokes `parse_string()` on bytes from the staged reader buffer.

evidence_limitations: The staged vulnerable workspace inside the running ARVO container (`/src/jsoncons`) is at commit `5a5a972253990361f19fa64f08b49ba4677944ae`, not the metadata's `b453dc0b9204685c9058f0000639c2764961aba6`. This GT grounds all lines and code snippets to the staged source that Stage 01 actually compiled and crashed on, while retaining the metadata commits as sample provenance.

The bundled `patch.diff` comes from a nearby source snapshot of `json_encoder.hpp`; it shows the same logical fix (`it = r.ptr - 1`) but does not textually match the staged vulnerable file line-for-line. The causal chain here is therefore anchored to the staged vulnerable source and saved ASan trace, using the patch only to confirm the missing iterator adjustment.

coarse_trace.summary: The reader loads the full 29-byte PoC into its vector buffer, resizes that vector to logical size 29, and points the parser at the same storage, creating the container boundary later crossed at offset 29.
The parser enters the first object member-name string, does not reject raw `0x7f`, and materializes the key slice at `buffer_.data() + 2` with length 20 when it reaches the closing quote.
The parser wraps that slice in a `string_view`, validates it, and dispatches it as an object key through `visitor.key()`.
The key encoder forwards the same `(pointer,length)` pair into `jsoncons::detail::escape_string()`.

On the final visited `0x7f`, the buggy `it = r.ptr` update leaves `it == end`, the loop header skips to the trailing `:[true` bytes, and the `it != end` condition keeps line 52 executing until it reaches `buffer_.data() + 29`, where the saved container-overflow read occurs.

fine_trace.note: Source. The `stream_source` wrapped around the fuzz target's `std::istringstream` copies the entire saved witness into `buffer_`. For this PoC, `count == 29` and bytes `buffer_[0..28]` are exactly `{`, `"`, twenty key bytes, the closing quote, `:`, `[`, `t`, `r`, `u`, `e`.

The vector's logical size becomes 29 while the constructor's earlier `buffer_.reserve(16384)` keeps the larger container in place. That makes `buffer_.data() + 29` the first byte outside the active range, matching the saved ASan address.

The witness has no BOM, so `offset == 0`. `parser_.update()` therefore makes the parser read directly from the same vector buffer: `begin_input_ = buffer_.data()`, `input_end_ = buffer_.data() + 29`, and `input_ptr_ = begin_input_`.

When `parse_string()` reaches the closing quote at `buffer_[22]`, it passes the member-name slice `s = buffer_.data() + 2`, `length = 20` into `end_string_value()`. `JSONCONS_ILLEGAL_CONTROL_CHARACTER` only covers `0x00..0x1f`, so the raw `0x7f` bytes in `buffer_[2..21]` survived unchanged to this point.

Wraps that member-name slice without copying. `sv.data()` still points at `buffer_.data() + 2`, `sv.length()` is 20, and bytes 22..28 remain in the same underlying reader buffer immediately after the slice.

`unicode_traits::validate(s, length)` accepts the same bytes, and because `parent() == json_parse_state::member_name`, the parser dispatches this exact `string_view` into the key-encoding visitor path seen in the saved crash stack.
`visit_key()` forwards the same pointer and length into `escape_string()`. The encoder is therefore walking bytes inside the reader buffer, not a copied key string.

Computes the key-slice bound `end == buffer_.data() + 22`. The bytes after that bound in the same 29-byte buffer are `buffer_[22]='"'`, `buffer_[23]=':'`, `buffer_[24]='['`, `buffer_[25]='t'`, `buffer_[26]='r'`, `buffer_[27]='u'`, and `buffer_[28]='e'`.

On iterations that land on raw `0x7f` bytes inside the key, this dereference yields `c == 0x7f`, so execution enters the control-character branch. In the saved layout, the earlier buggy jump from `buffer_[19]` lands on the final key byte `buffer_[21] == 0x7f`, so the same path executes on `end - 1`.

fine_trace.code: auto r = unicode_traits::to_codepoint(it, end, cp, unicode_traits::conv_flags::strict);
fine_trace.note: For ASCII DEL, `to_codepoint()` consumes exactly one byte and returns `cp == 0x7f`, `r.ec == conv_errc()`, and `r.ptr == it + 1`; on the final key byte at `buffer_[21]`, that means `r.ptr == end`.

Root cause. The loop stores the first post-codepoint address in `it` even though the `for` header will still execute `++it`. On the final key byte, this leaves `it == end == buffer_.data() + 22`, which already points past the 20-byte key slice and at the closing quote.

fine_trace.code: for (const CharT* it = begin; it != end; ++it)
fine_trace.note: The loop header then applies its own increment, moving `it` from `end` to `buffer_.data() + 23` and skipping the closing quote at `buffer_[22]`. Because the guard is only `it != end`, once `it > end` the loop will not terminate on the key bound anymore.

The first dereference after leaving the key slice reads `buffer_[23] == ':'`. This read is already outside the 20-byte `string_view` but still inside the 29-byte reader buffer, so ASan does not fire yet.

fine_trace.code: for (const CharT* it = begin; it != end; ++it)
fine_trace.note: Since `:` and the following `[` `t` `r` `u` `e` bytes are ordinary non-control characters, the body stays on the plain copy path and the same header keeps advancing `it` through `buffer_[24]` .. `buffer_[28]` and then to `buffer_.data() + 29` while `it != end` remains true.

Sink. When `it == buffer_.data() + 29`, line 52 dereferences the first byte past the vector's 29-byte logical size. The saved ASan report places the fault at `0x62900000021d`, i.e. 29 bytes into the 16384-byte region reserved for this reader buffer.

poc.trigger: Run the saved 29-byte file through `fuzz_json_encoder`. `json_reader` loads it into a 29-byte vector buffer, the parser accepts bytes 2..21 as the first member-name key, and `escape_string()`'s buggy `it = r.ptr` update on the final visited `0x7f` makes the loop skip out of that key, walk the trailing `:[true` bytes, and then dereference `buffer_.data() + 29`, triggering the saved container-overflow before EOF handling for the truncated JSON suffix.

format.name: JSON
format.contract: The saved witness is exactly `7b 22 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 3a 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f 22 3a 5b 74 72 75 65`. It must reach `parse_string()` with a 20-byte first member-name slice at offsets 2..21 ending in raw `0x7f`, followed in the same reader buffer by the bytes `22 3a 5b 74 72 75 65` (`":[true`). That exact layout is what lets the buggy loop leave the key slice, traverse the remaining in-buffer bytes, and hit the first out-of-container byte at offset 29.
